question: Will front-month ICE Brent crude futures (January 2027 contract) settle above $100.00 per barrel on 27 November 2026?

calls.reasoning: Jan-27 Brent settled $95.15 on Nov 16 (~$95.3 on Nov 17); YES needs a >5.1% gain (log 0.0497) in 9 sessions. Under a driftless random walk with 40-55% annualized vol (recent realized: >$107 on Nov 2-3, sub-$90 intraday ~Nov 10-11), P(9-day move > +5%) is about 25-33%. Bearish: IEA's 1.7 mb/d Q4 surplus, Hormuz flows largely recovered, weak China demand, SPR releases, -13% over the month. Bullish tail: unverified tanker mine strikes reported by Iran and fragile US-Iran talks, with single headlines moving price 3%+. No matching human market: Kalshi lists Nov 30 Brent contracts at ~$102/$104 thresholds but I couldn't see prices; a Polymarket/Kalshi weekly lists only WTI contracts. Shading slightly below the vol-implied midpoint for the de-escalation drift.
calls.dossier:
- ICE Brent Jan-27 (front month) settled $95.15 on Mon Nov 16, 2026, down 69c (CNBC, Nov 16). It traded about $95.3 early Nov 17 (search snippet). Earlier settles from the question background: $95.82 on Nov 12, $91.49 on Nov 10 (a 10-week low, with a brief intraday dip below $90 on Trump saying the Iran war could end 'fairly soon' per financefeeds), about $98.32 a week before that. Brent traded $107+ on Nov 2-3 (search summary).
- Distance to threshold: $100.00 is +5.1% from $95.15 (log 0.0497).
- Bearish drivers (CNBC/HDFC Sky, Nov 16): IEA forecasts a 1.7 mb/d global surplus in Q4 2026; October inventories rose 52 mb, the first monthly build since June; global supply 105.4 mb/d; Hormuz shipments largely back to pre-conflict levels; China October refinery runs -2% m/m and -8.1% y/y; 71 mb of emergency reserves available by Feb 2027; US Jones Act waiver extended. Trading Economics: Brent -13.4% over the past month, +47.8% y/y; November average so far about $96.9 vs $123.9 in October.
- Bullish drivers: IRGC/Iranian state media say 2 tankers hit mines and 6 more caught fire over the weekend of Nov 14-15 (Reuters could not verify). Analysts say physical constraints dominate until a US-Iran settlement. Earlier, Brent jumped about 3% in a day when Iran denied talks with Washington (oilprice.com headline). Freight rates remain elevated.
- EIA STEO (Nov 10): expects Brent near $100 for the rest of 2026; 2026 average $97.44.
- OPEC+ full ministerial on Nov 29, after the settlement date. Thanksgiving is Thu Nov 26 (US holiday; ICE Europe trades, possibly thin).
- Vol reference: the recent regime shows multi-percent daily moves both ways. The $107 to $91.5 slide took about a week. An assumed 40-55% annualized vol gives a 9-session 1-sd move of roughly 7.6-10.5%.
- Status-quo outcome: price stays in the $90-97 range, which would resolve NO.
- Resolves off the ICE official settlement for BRN Jan-27 on Fri Nov 27 (Barchart CBF27 row as display; ICE governs). Not off spot, Dated Brent, an intraday high, or Kalshi's Nov 30 price.
- Event window: a single settlement on 2026-11-27. As of Nov 17 00:20Z, 9 trading sessions remain (Nov 17-27).
- Searched but not found: prices for Kalshi's Brent contracts (Kalshi lists Nov 30 Brent contracts at about $101.99/$103.99 thresholds); no Polymarket or Manifold Brent $100 contract for Nov 27; no options-implied vol figure for Jan-27 Brent.

calls.reconciliation: The main factual dispute is the current price level: Run 1 had a $95.15 Nov 16 settle, Run 3 had ~$92-94. The settle at $95.15 (down 69c from $95.84) is internally consistent with the Reuters/CNBC reports. Run 3's lower prints are timestamped after the 19:28 London settlement window, so they likely reflect post-settle weakness. Without web access I couldn't verify them, so I used ~$93-94 as the effective start with uncertainty either way. Vol assumptions converge on a 9-10% 9-day sigma. All runs saw the same bearish fundamentals; I applied a modest downward shade from the ~24% driftless figure. The Kalshi snippet was unverified and settles off a different date, so it was not used.
